title: Audit logs: redact sensitive fields in event payloads (no secrets/tokens)
author: Hanae Suzuki
description: Context: Audit events frequently include request/actor metadata and (in some code paths) arbitrary parameter blobs; because audit logs are exportable to customer-controlled sinks, we must guarantee secrets/tokens never appear in persisted/exported payloads. This PR adds centralized redaction rules to the shared audit logging library and enforces them via tests so sensitive keys are scrubbed before enqueue/persist/export. Changes: add a deterministic deep-redaction walker (maps + arrays) with key-based matching and a small set of header/value heuristics; redact values to "[REDACTED]" while preserving payload shape; include safeguards to avoid over-redacting common non-secret fields (e.g. token_count, api_token_id). Tests: add unit tests covering nested payloads, arrays, mixed casing, headers, and regression cases discovered during enterprise questionnaire review. Rollout: this is non-breaking; it only mutates payload values for sensitive keys and emits a metric when redaction occurs to help identify upstream callers still passing secrets.
commits: auditlog: introduce payload redactor + default rule set
auditlog: apply redaction prior to validation/enqueue
tests: add redaction suite for nested maps/arrays + header keys
metrics: emit auditlog_redaction_applied counter w/ key category
docs: note payload redaction guarantees + guidance for service owners
notable_implementation_details: Redaction runs in-process in the shared emitter prior to schema validation and enqueue, so secrets are never written to the audit pipeline or DLQ. Matching is primarily key-based (case-insensitive, underscore/hyphen tolerant) for common secret-bearing fields: password, secret, client_secret, api_key, x_api_key, token, access_token, refresh_token, id_token, bearer, authorization, private_key, signing_key, session, cookie, set_cookie. A secondary heuristic redacts header values if the header key is Authorization or starts with X-Api-Key, and redacts string values that look like "Bearer <...>" when paired with an auth-ish key. The walker preserves object structure and array length and replaces only leaf values; non-string primitives are replaced with "[REDACTED]" as a string to keep JSON export stable. To prevent over-redaction, the rules explicitly exclude keys like token_count, token_usage, api_token_id, key_id, rotation_id where values are identifiers/metrics rather than credentials. Depth/size limits: traversal caps at 50 levels and 10k nodes to avoid pathological payloads; on cap hit we redact the remainder and increment a metric.
tests_summary: Added a table-driven suite validating: (1) nested objects (maps inside maps) are redacted for sensitive keys; (2) arrays of objects are traversed and redacted; (3) mixed casing (Access_Token vs accessToken) and separators (api-key vs api_key) are matched; (4) headers objects redact Authorization and cookie-like keys; (5) regression: token_count remains unmodified; (6) regression: api_token_id remains unmodified; (7) large payload triggers cap behavior and is still safe (no secrets leak).
review_conversation: Marcus Lin (Security): Please confirm this runs before persistence/export (including DLQ) and add a unit test proving Authorization header values are redacted. Also ensure we don’t accidentally redact api_token_id (identifier) because support uses it for investigations. Hanae Suzuki (author): Updated to run before validator/enqueue and added tests for Authorization and api_token_id exclusion; also added auditlog_redaction_applied metric to help find callers still passing secrets. Allison Grant (Observability): Prefer emitting a counter rather than logs; also ensure redaction is deterministic so exporters don’t flap due to ordering. Hanae Suzuki: Added counter with labels (category=header|payload, key_group=token|secret|password) and kept deterministic traversal by sorting map keys before visiting. Nadia Rahman (Telemetry): Any perf concerns? This will run on every sensitive action. Hanae Suzuki: Traversal is linear in payload size; added depth/node caps and only runs on payload/metadata (not on message body streaming paths). Kaitlyn Nguyen (Auth/RBAC): Can we explicitly redact cookie / set-cookie? Hanae Suzuki: Added cookie + set_cookie keys to rule set and included tests for both spellings.
release_notes: Security: Audit log payloads are now centrally redacted for secret/token-bearing fields prior to persistence/export; added tests to prevent regressions.
merge_outcome: Merged into main; no rollout flags required (library change).
